artifact.primary_cause: The Tuesday figure was produced by a read that landed inside a mart rebuild. daily_revenue_load for 2026-03-02 failed at 05:00, 06:00 and 07:00 because the vendor bundle had not arrived, and finally succeeded at 08:14:49. Its completion triggered an off-schedule rebuild of the revenue mart at 08:14:58, and pipelines/bi_extract.sql fired on its normal quarter-hour tick at 08:15:00, two seconds in. mart_rebuild.sql publishes the fact and the dimension as two separate rename pairs, so for the moment between them the catalog held the NEW fact against the PREVIOUS build's dimension. That earlier dimension still carried two rows for 883 of the 1,180 reseller accounts onboarded on 2026-02-25 - a duplication that had been harmless for a week because those accounts had no revenue until the channel launched on 2026-03-02, and the lines for that launch arrived in the very bundle that had just landed. The join fanned them out and counted their first day twice. The reported month-to-date figure was 15,385,785.19 against a true 13,482,810.23; the excess of 1,902,974.96 is exactly the new resellers' 2026-03-02 revenue. No table in the warehouse was wrong, then or now - the mart was correct before the read and correct after it, and the same bundle that exposed the duplicated dimension rows also removed them from raw.customer_master.

artifact.repair_strategy: Three things. (1) Reverted the DATA-5518 predicate in pipelines/mart_rebuild.sql and republished the mart. The mart was never double counting - the reported number was - and the predicate silently removed the entire reseller segment, 17,473 rows, from every historical figure the mart produces, which is why revenue has looked low since 2026-03-03 17:07. (2) Merged the APAC rate redelivery that was sitting unmerged in raw.fx_rates_inbox and reconverted staging. raw.fx_rates_daily had no JPY rows from 2026-02-16, and stg_revenue_lines resolves the rate AS OF the order date, so every APAC line since then converted at the 2026-02-15 rate and overstated the region by 8.7 per cent. That is separate from Tuesday and is why APAC has looked wrong for longer. (3) Wrapped the mart publish in one transaction and made it re-runnable with drop-if-exists guards. Verified on this engine that a reader on another connection sees the pre-publish state until COMMIT, so the window between the two rename pairs is no longer observable. The extract is unchanged: making it a single statement would not have helped, because the half-published catalog is visible to whatever resolves the names while it exists. warehouse.rev_snapshot has been restated at the one tick and nowhere else - it is the record Finance quotes from, so the APAC error in the older rows stays, because that is genuinely what was reported at the time.
supporting_evidence: warehouse.mart_revenue_dim__dbt_backup is the previous build's dimension, left behind because the interrupted publish never ran its final DROP; it holds 11,063 rows against the live dimension's 10,180, and the surplus is exactly one extra row for each of 883 accounts, all of them from onboarding batch cm-20260225-0001 but only three quarters of it - no predicate on the live tables picks that set out
